verdict.rationale: Viam documents local data queuing during network outages, automatic sync when connectivity returns, and automatic handling of restarts and storage constraints. Its SDKs also reconnect automatically when the network drops, and ML models run inference locally on the machine. However, no evidence explicitly states that machine control logic keeps operating fully while the cloud is unreachable. A community comment that the robot firmware assumes internet access is an early read rather than a concrete hands-on failure, so it lowers confidence without creating a dispute. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that robots continue autonomous operation offline, details on buffer limits and recovery behavior, and independent or hands-on corroboration of offline buffering and clean recovery.

support.subject: As an ops lead, my robots keep operating and buffer data locally when cloud connectivity drops, then recover cleanly

citations.quote: Data queues locally during network outages and in low-bandwidth environments, and syncs when connectivity returns. Viam handles restarts and storage constraints automatically.
reconnect automatically when the network drops
Machines pull them automatically and run inference locally.
